name: Sarah Flannery

early_history_summary: Flannery grew up in County Cork, Ireland, and was encouraged in mathematics by her father David Flannery, a mathematics lecturer. She attended an evening math enrichment class taught by her father, which led to a work-experience placement at Baltimore Technologies where she was shown an unpublished cryptographic scheme by Michael Purser. She developed the Cayley-Purser algorithm based on matrix multiplication, presented it at the Young Scientist Exhibition, and won both the Irish and European titles.
family_context_summary: Father David Flannery was a mathematics lecturer at Cork Institute of Technology who taught Sarah mathematics from a young age and encouraged her interest in the subject.

Her father, a mathematics lecturer, taught her mathematics from childhood and ran the evening enrichment class that connected her to Baltimore Technologies, where she was given Michael Purser's unpublished cryptographic scheme to implement. The algorithm was later found to be flawed as a public-key system, but the achievement was widely reported and recognized.

He presented at the 2007 Intel ISEF and had a minor planet named after him.

name: Nima Arkani-Hamed
milestone_by_age_26: Co-authored the ADD model (Arkani-Hamed, Dimopoulos, Dvali) in 1998 at age 26, proposing large extra dimensions as a solution to the hierarchy problem, which became one of the most cited papers in particle physics and reshaped the field's approach to physics beyond the Standard Model.
early_history_summary: Arkani-Hamed was born on April 5, 1972, in Houston, Texas, to Jafargholi 'Jafar' Arkani-Hamed and Hamideh Alasti, both physicists from Iran. His father worked for the NASA Apollo program and later taught earth and planetary sciences at McGill University. The family moved to Toronto, where Nima graduated from the University of Toronto with a joint honours degree in mathematics and physics in 1993. He earned his PhD from UC Berkeley in 1997 under Lawrence Hall, then became a postdoc at SLAC. In 1998, while at SLAC, he co-authored the ADD model with Savas Dimopoulos and Gia Dvali, proposing that gravity's weakness is due to large extra spatial dimensions.

trajectory.event: Won the top prize at the Science Talent Search as a Stuyvesant High School student.
Earned BA from Harvard University.
Completed PhD at Princeton under Frank Wilczek; co-discovered non-Abelian statistics associated with Majorana zero modes.
Became professor of physics at UCLA.
Joined Microsoft; co-authored proposal for topological qubit with Freedman and Das Sarma.
Became director and general manager of Microsoft Station Q.
Team unveiled the Majorana 1 chip, an eight-qubit topological processor.
